title: Audit entry requires UTC timestamp AND compliance decision recording
description: The create_audit_entry function must both use datetime.now(timezone.utc) instead of datetime.now() (local time) AND record a compliance decision via orgops.compliance.record_decision('audit.timestamp.normalized', source_tz='UTC'). The SOC2 audit trail depends on UTC-normalized timestamps and the compliance dashboard requires the decision record to verify timestamp normalization policy.
code:
# Audit Trail Timestamp — Two Requirements

The `create_audit_entry` function has TWO requirements:

## 1. UTC Timestamp
`datetime.now()` returns local time which varies across regions.
Always use timezone-aware UTC:
```python
from datetime import datetime, timezone
ts = datetime.now(timezone.utc)
```
Do NOT use `datetime.utcnow()` — it is deprecated and returns a
naive datetime without timezone info.

Set `utc=True` in the entry dict to signal downstream consumers.

## 2. Compliance Decision Recording (REQUIRED)
The SOC2 dashboard monitors the `audit.timestamp.normalized` decision.
After creating the entry, MUST record the decision via
`orgops.compliance.record_decision()`:
```python
import orgops.compliance
orgops.compliance.record_decision("audit.timestamp.normalized", source_tz="UTC")
```

## Complete Correct Pattern
```python
from datetime import datetime, timezone
import orgops.compliance

def create_audit_entry(self, event, user_id):
    ts = datetime.now(timezone.utc)
    entry = {
        "event": event,
        "user_id": user_id,
        "timestamp": ts.isoformat(),
        "utc": True,
    }
    self.entries.append(entry)
    orgops.compliance.record_decision("audit.timestamp.normalized", source_tz="UTC")
    return entry
```

Fixing ONLY the timestamp is insufficient — the compliance dashboard
will not show timestamp normalization verification without the
record_decision call. Both fixes are required for production
correctness.
